record.label: Native-frame corrector refit (collective tape)
record.summary: Refit the deployed card's F2J transport corrector with THREE collective-tracker features added to its input tape (raw20 -> 23), computed from the card's OWN states (native frame, train/deploy consistent; export verified: L12 K3S 9.88 vs 9.92). PRIOR: the aug-7 F2Q arm measured null (+0.10%) with the preregistered wrong-frame caveat - 'the native-frame instance resolves that ambiguity'; this IS that instance, and its channels encode the measured dominant deficit (the card carries 1.5% of collective kappa3) rather than generic observables (aug-7 max residual-correlation 0.046). Feature generation running (688 nets, 4 CPU workers, ~26 s/net).
record.terminal_criterion: Refit OOF materially beats the F2J baseline AND the packaged card clears a meaningful adjusted gain on the 8-net panel - or a measured null that, being native-frame, closes the information-cap question honestly.

evidence.claim: SENTINEL-FAIL (honest null): fold-0 refit 3.1100e-8 vs matched baseline 3.1543e-8 = -1.40% under the preregistered halve gate; native-frame resolution of the aug-7 F2Q wrong-frame caveat - the collective tape adds ~nothing the corrector can use
evidence.receipt_status: legacy descriptive reference; not current graph authority

record.goal_path_summary:
The deployed card = a physics engine plus a learned corrector that removes 69% of the engine's error. Every attempt to hand-inject our collective-skewness discovery into the engine made things worse, because the corrector was trained around the old engine. This node does it the right way round: give the CORRECTOR the collective information as three new input signals and retrain it, so it learns how to use what the card is missing (98.5% of the biggest known error).
A similar idea with generic signals failed before - but with a recorded caveat that wrong-frame signals made the test ambiguous, and ours are exactly the right-frame version aimed at a specific measured hole. If the refit works, it goes straight through the local screen and the 8-network panel to a submission; if it fails, it settles honestly whether the corrector is information-capped.
RESOLVED 08-31: sentinel-fail at -1.40%. The corrector information-cap question is closed in the native frame: collective-tracker features do not move the corrector. Raw gains must come from in-card closure physics, not corrector inputs.
